 Royals Exercise Club Option On Tony Gonsolin, Decline Carlos Estévez
 By Darragh McDonald |
 at October 29, 2026 4:05pm CDT 
 The Royals announced that they have exercised a 2027 club option on right-hander Tony Gonsolin . He will make $2.5MM next year. Right-hander Carlos Estévez has had his $13MM club option turned down. He becomes a free agent and collects a $2MM buyout.
 Gonsolin is a relatively low-cost wild card for next year’s staff. From 2019 to 2023, he tossed 375 2/3 innings for the Dodgers, allowing 3.19 earned runs per nine. He had a 23.1% strikeout rate, 8.7% walk rate and 38.8% ground ball rate.
 He hasn’t been much of a factor since then. He required Tommy John surgery in August of 2023, wiping out the end of that season and his 2024 campaign. In 2025, he suffered a back injury while lifting weights. He began the season on the injured list. He came off the IL in April, made seven starts with an ERA of 5.00, then returned to the IL with elbow discomfort. He would eventually require internal brace surgery in August.
 He was bumped from the Dodgers roster after the season. He was still recovering from his surgery when the 2026 campaign began. He didn’t sign until August. The Royals gave him a prorated $1MM salary and a $2.5MM club option for 2027. He made four minor league rehab appearances before joining the big league club. He made one appearance in the majors, allowing five earned runs in 2 2/3 innings, before an allergic reaction put him back on the IL in late September.
 Gonsolin didn’t do much to impress in 2026. His velocity was sitting in the low 90s, a few ticks below where it was during his time with the Dodgers. But the Royals will hope he can get back on track next year as he is further removed from his injury woes.
 The rotation could certainly use some help. Guys like Cole Ragans , Stephen Kolek , Ryan Bergert , Luinder Avila and Ben Kudrna are going to be recovering from surgery when the 2027 season begins, cutting into the depth. They will have Michael Wacha , Seth Lugo and Noah Cameron in three spots. Randy Dobnak and Daniel Lynch IV are currently options for the back end. Gonsolin will try to provide them with another option. If his injury odyssey leads to workload restrictions, perhaps he could end up in the bullpen instead.
 The decision on Estévez isn’t a surprise. The Royals signed him to a two-year deal going into 2025. At the time, he was one of the better closers in the league. In 2025, his 2.45 ERA was still good but his strikeout rate dropped from 23.6% the year prior to just 20.1%, while his walk rate climbed from 5.7% to 8.2%. He had some help keeping the ERA low, as his .234 batting average on balls in play and 77.6% strand rate were both to the fortunate side. His 3.67 FIP and 4.43 SIERA were skeptical.
 Then his 2026 was marred by injuries. He did make one appearance to start the year but allowed six earned runs in a third of an inning. He was hit by a comebacker in the process and was placed on the IL with a left foot contusion. While on a rehab assignment, he suffered a rotator cuff strain. He underwent surgery in September with an uncertain timeline.
 Given his recent results and health issues, the Royals weren’t going to give him $13MM for next year. His next contract will likely depend on his recovery. He will turn 34 in late December, which will likely be during the upcoming lockout.
